issues.description: The problem statement and the solution use a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template Stock implementation provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This naming mismatch for the same conceptual operation (clearing/emptying the stock) can confuse students: they may look for emptyStock() as described in the specification or in the UML and not find it in the template, or implement emptyStock() while the template already has clearInventory().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the template's clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or update the problem statement and solution to refer to clearInventory(). Alternatively, add an emptyStock() wrapper in the template that delegates to clearInventory() (or vice versa) so both method names are available and the UML/spec match the code.
